summary: I checked all 34 tests: keep 20, refute 14. I ran every mutation through `srdloop mutate`, so the repo is unchanged. Exact duplicates: Sacred Flame vs Total Cover, a Magic Missile dart vs Total Cover, the area-spell Total Cover case (all already in test_playing_the_game.py), Bless past its 3-target cap (already at test_spells.py:300) and Fire Bolt on a crate (scenario SPELLS-05). The Guiding Bolt Total Cover case runs the same check as an existing Magic Missile test. Wrong reason: three Hold Person tests ('does nothing to a beast', 'does nothing to a fey goblin', 'beast through the session') still pass with the creature-type check removed, because the seeded save happens to succeed. The 'refused target spends no slot' test still passes with the Total Cover rule removed, because the can-see check refuses the cast. The Spare the Dying test still passes with its 0-HP target check removed; it is also tied to the slot clause, but a cantrip uses no slot. Wrong oracle: the Thunderwave red test assumes the cube has to include an unnamed creature, but the caster could place the cube to leave it out. The Mage Armor 'visibly does nothing' red test picks one reading where the rules give two: an armored creature as an invalid target, or as a target you can't choose. No register ruling covers this, so it goes to a person (confidence 0.45). Every remaining green test failed under a mutation of the rule it names. The three remaining red tests (Light on a creature, one Cone on both sides, Sleep's Sphere) fail for the reason their tickets state, and their oracles match the SRD wording.

verdicts.reason: Wrong oracle. A 15-ft Cube from the caster can be placed in several ways. With MIALEE at (0,0), a cube covering x 5-15 and y -10..0 contains G1 (5,0) but not G2 (5,5). Naming only G1 is a legal placement, so 'G2 must take damage' doesn't follow from 'the area determines what the spell targets'. The engine takes no cube position or direction to settle it. A valid red test needs a creature that every legal placement containing the named one must also include, or an explicit placement.
verdicts.mutation: Red test: with --runxfail it fails at assert g2.hp == 3 (G2 untouched). That is the stated reason, but the expectation itself depends on an assumed cube placement.

verdicts.reason: Picks one reading of an open ambiguity with no register ruling. It treats 'a willing creature who isn't wearing armor' as an invalid target (slot spent, nothing happens). It could equally be a target you can't choose, which is how this batch treats Ray of Frost on an object and Light on a creature, and how test_mage_armor_..._isnt_a_half_refusal accepts it. The current refusal may be correct. A person should decide (propose a register row).
